report:
In the medial compartment, intra-meniscus increased signal without reaching the surface; contusions at posterior part of body to posterior horn.  There is diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along weight-baring medial femoral condyle. No osteophytes.  
  
 The lateral compartment, complex tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus with suspect for flip of the meniscus to intercondylar region.  Diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along weight-baring medial femoral condyle. No osteophytes.  
  
 The patellofemoral joint; appear congruent.  
 The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 The anterior cruciate ligaments are almost complete torn; midsubstance. There is no tibial translation.  
 posterior cruciate ligaments; buckling with low grade partial tear.  
  
 The medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are intact.  
  
 The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact. The popliteofibular ligament is intact.  
  
 Torn arcuate ligament with fluid along popliteus tendon.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Minimal amount of right knee effusion is present.  
  The surrounding musculature is normal. There is no fracture or bone contusion.  - ACL; almost complete torn 
 - PCL;  buckling with low grade partial tear 
 - Torn arcuate ligament with fluid along popliteus tendon.  
 - Medial meniscus, contusions at posterior part of body to posterior horn.   
 - Lateral compartment, complex tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus with suspect for flip of the meniscus to intercondylar region.

> MRI of left knee was performed in sagittal, axial and coronal sections.
> Spin echo sequence were used.

> There is a mass lesion in the posterior knee, measuring about 5.8x2.0x1.8 cm in size, arising 
  between medial gastronemius tendon and the semimembranous tendon head with iso-signal intensity 
  on T1WI and hyper-signal intensity on T2WI compatible with Baker's cyst ans associated with 
  adjacent soft tissue infiltrations.
> The contour of ACL is in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 
  1 injury.
> There are increased intrasubsance signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus and 
  anterior horn of lateral meniscus on proton density sequence, R/O tear.
> Massive effusions in suprapatellar bursa and with suspicious some irregular multiple villous 
  lipomatous synovial proliferations, in favor of massive effusion with synovitis with/without 
  lipoma arborescence.
> Subcutaneous infiltration is noted at infrapatellar area to pretibial area.
> Presence of fissure of medial aspect lateral facet of patella extending to subchondral 
  bone in favor of grade 2 chondromalacia.
> The contour of PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial and lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.

Impression: 
1. Compatible with a Baker's cyst associated with adjacent soft tissue infiltrations.
2. Massive effusion with synovitis and with/without lipoma arborescence.
3. In favor of grade 2 chondromalacia of medial aspect lateral facet of patella.
4. Suspected tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus and anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

FINDINGS:

Fractures:
None.

Joint alignment:
Normal.

Degenerative changes:
Focal high to full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral femoral condyle and tibia posteriorly. This is most likely related to a prior osteochondral injury.

Mild cartilage loss in the patellofemoral cartilage with thinning of the patellar cartilage inferiorly.

Bone marrow signal:
Normal. Subchondral cysts involving the lateral tibial plateau.

Anterior cruciate ligament: Mild signal abnormality involving the ACL ligament at the posterior insertion to the femur, likely related to a mild sprain.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Normal.
Medial collateral ligament: Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: The fibular collateral ligament, IT band and biceps femoris are intact. Signal abnormality involving the popliteus tendon insertion at the lateral femoral condyle, most likely tendinosis. The popliteomeniscal fascicles are not well seen and likely torn, with associated mild medial displacement of the popliteus tendon below the popliteus hiatus.

Medial meniscus: Normal.
Lateral meniscus: Complex multidirectional tear involving the posterior, body and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is volume loss in the body and a large displaced fragment in the intercondylar notch. There is complete loss of tissue in the posterior horn, likely a complete radial tear. There is unusual U shaped fragment adjacent to the posterior root ligament.

Extensor mechanism: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Normal.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Normal.

Joint effusion: Small to moderate right knee joint effusion, with synovial thickening. There is a small loose body in the suprapatellar recess measuring approximately 3 mm.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Complex multidirectional tear of the body, posterior and anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, with a large unusually shaped displaced fragment in the intercondylar notch. Recommend an orthopedic surgery consultation.
*Mild signal abnormality of the ACL, likely from a sprain, without evidence of tear.
*Focal high to full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral compartment posteriorly, most significantly the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

Findings:  Large joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments. Prominent bursa deep to the MCL.  Complex degenerate tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a full-thickness radial component of the body and a superiorly displaced component adjacent to the posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle (see image snap shot). Intact lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, distal iliotibial band and pes anserine tendons. Small ganglion around the popliteus tendon.  Intact extensor mechanism. No evidence of fat pad impingement.  High-grade chondral thinning in the weightbearing portion of the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Focal high-grade chondropathy in the lateral tibial condyle with minor underlying bone stress change. High-grade chondral thinning and full-thickness chondral loss across the majority of the medial and lateral retropatellar facets. Full-thickness chondral loss is also noted in the lateral aspect of the lateral femoral trochlea groove with underlying bone stress change.  
Conclusion:  Large knee joint effusion. Complex tear of the medial meniscus as described above. MCL bursa. Tricompartmental degenerative change, prominent in the patellofemoral compartment. Ancillary findings described above.
